children: Piper Sandler initiated coverage on seven major semiconductor stocks, with most receiving strong ratings as the artificial intelligence market is "starving for more compute capacity."
The financial services firm assigned Overweight ratings to AMD
. Broadcom and Nvidia were named "top picks" for their accelerators, while AMD and Arm were highlighted for gaining market share in CPU servers. Intel
The high ratings were applied to those Piper Sandler contends are playing the most significant role in the hyperscaler and neocloud buildout.

"Compute is arguably the key enabler of AI, and with the takeoff of Agentic, AI is starving for more compute capacity," said Piper Sandler analysts David O'Connor and Zackary Altman in an in-depth investor report. "2027 is already sold-out, and order books are full for 2028. We estimate a Compute market of $2.2T by 2030, o/w $2T for Accelerators and $0.2T for CPU's. This 5x of the Compute market by 2030 is driving top-line expansion for the Compute enablers and translating into an average of ~45% EPS CAGR across the group."
The investment firm applied a $600 price target to AMD, $320 to Arm, $460 to Broadcom, $110 to Intel, $270 to Marvell, $300 to Nvidia and $190 to Qualcomm.

"The current scarcity of Compute is plainly visible in GPU hourly pricing for NeoClouds," O'Connor noted. "Silicon Data's H100 pricing index shows the Nvidia H100 GPU pricing per hour at $2.60 per hour vs. $2.00 in December—immediately before the occurrence of OpenClaw. Interestingly, in Feb. '25 we also saw a spike in demand owing to strengthening demand from DeepSeek being deployed—lower cost equates to more use, driving demand higher again. We'd like to call out that the H100 was launched by Nvidia—in volume—back in Q4 '22, meaning the tech is already nearly 4 years old."

In addition to the rising demand, component costs have also increased, driving revenue higher for hardware companies. Piper Sandler finds the GPU chip cost increased from 30% to 40% over the last two generations.

title: Piper Sandler initiates semi stocks with high ratings as market is 'starving for compute'
